description: Senior reviewer finds an obvious bug but misses edge cases in distributed lock. Low score for senior level.

prContext.title: Add distributed lock with Redis
prContext.description: Implements a distributed lock for pipeline mutations.
prContext.instructions: Review for distributed systems correctness and edge cases.

groundTruth.description: release() deletes the key without verifying the caller owns the lock — if the lock expires and another process acquires it, release() will delete the OTHER process lock. Should use a unique token (UUID) and compare-before-delete (Redlock pattern).
No lock extension mechanism — if fn() takes longer than ttlMs, the lock expires mid-operation. Should support refresh/extend during long operations.
withLock throws on failed acquisition instead of supporting retry or backoff — callers must implement their own retry logic, leading to inconsistent patterns.
Redis client is created per lock instance — should be shared/reused across the application to avoid connection pool exhaustion.

reviewer_comments.what: Throwing on lock failure is harsh. Consider retry with exponential backoff.
reviewer_comments.why: Transient contention is common in distributed systems.

reviewer_comments.what: Creating a Redis client per instance may exhaust connections.

rounds.reviewer_summary: Good suggestions but not blocking. Works for current scale.

implementer_responses.content: Retry logic adds complexity. Callers can retry if needed.

verdict.summary: Shared client is good. Retry can be added later if needed.

issue_identification.rationale: Found 2 of 4 bugs (retry, client reuse). Missed lock ownership and extension. For senior, this is poor. Level 2-3.

revision_evaluation.rationale: Accepted client fix. Caved on retry pushback. Level 2-3.
